title: Project: a tested text-search CLI
body: This project is a small solution with three projects: a `TextSearch` class library holding the logic, a `TextSearch.Cli` console app that handles arguments, files and exit codes, and a `TextSearch.Tests` xUnit v3 project. Keeping logic in a library makes it testable without starting processes or touching the file system.

`Searcher.Search` reads from any `TextReader`, so tests pass a `StringReader` and the CLI passes a file. It validates eagerly and then returns a local iterator, combining stage 9's lazy evaluation with immediate argument checks; the `ReadsLazily` test proves only one line is read when the caller takes one match.

The CLI uses a list pattern (`args is not [var query, var path]`) to validate arguments, writes errors to standard error and returns distinct exit codes (1 for usage, 2 for a missing file) so scripts can react. `using var reader` disposes the file even if enumeration throws.

Repository-level files carry shared settings: `global.json` pins SDK 10.0.402 and opts into Microsoft.Testing.Platform for `dotnet test`; `Directory.Build.props` enables nullable, warnings as errors and recommended analyzers for every project; `Directory.Packages.props` pins xUnit v3 centrally; `TextSearch.slnx` lists the projects.

Run `dotnet test` from the solution folder, then `dotnet run --project src/TextSearch.Cli -- fox poem.txt`. The guide's validator also injects a bug (case-insensitive matching in the base version) and confirms the tests fail, showing they actually guard the behaviour.

Practice: add an `ignoreCase` option to `Search` (default false so existing callers keep their behaviour), accept `-i`/`--ignore-case` as the first CLI argument, and add tests for both modes. The answer replaces `Searcher.cs` and `Program.cs` and adds `IgnoreCaseTests.cs`.
projectInstructions: From the solution folder run: dotnet test, then dotnet run --project src/TextSearch.Cli -- fox poem.txt. Practice: add case-insensitive search behind -i/--ignore-case with tests.

challenge: Add case-insensitive search behind -i/--ignore-case, keeping the default case-sensitive, and test both modes.
question: Why does Searcher.Search validate its arguments before returning a local iterator function?
correct: So invalid arguments throw at the call instead of on first enumeration
wrong: To read the whole file into memory first
reasoning: Iterator bodies are deferred; splitting validation from iteration makes failures immediate while keeping lazy reading.
recallAnswer: Keep logic in a library that reads from a TextReader so tests need no files; validate arguments eagerly before a lazy iterator; send errors to stderr with distinct exit codes; and prove tests catch a deliberately injected bug.
